messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Telugu, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Telugu line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
కాని నీవు ఎందుకు అంత పెద్ద విసుగుకు తిరిగి వస్తున్నావు? ఎందుకు నీవు ఆ రుచికరమైన పర్వతాన్ని ఎక్కడం లేదు? అది మొత్తం ఆనందానికి మూలం మరియు కారణమా?

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (Telugu) | Back‑Translation (Eng.) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|------------------------------|--------------------------|--------| | Ma | adversative conjunction “but” | **కాని** | “but” | OK | | tu | 2nd person singular pronoun, subject | **నీవు** | “you” | OK | | perché | interrogative adverb “why” | **ఎందుకు** | “why” | OK | | ritorni | verb “return” (2nd sg.) | **తిరిగి వస్తున్నావు** | “you are returning” | OK | | a | preposition “to” (goal) | **కు** | “to” | OK | | tanta | high‑degree adjective “so great” | **అంత పెద్ద** | “so great” | OK | | noia | noun “annoyance / boredom” | **విసుగు** | “annoyance / boredom” | OK | | perché | interrogative adverb “why” (second question) | **ఎందుకు** | “why” | OK | | non | negative particle “not” | **లేదు** | “not” | OK | | sali | verb “you climb / ascend” (2nd sg.) | **ఎక్కడం** | “to climb” | OK | | il | definite article (masc. sg.) – not lexical in Telugu | *(omitted)* | – | **UNNECESSARY** | | dilettoso | adjective “delightful / delectable” | **రుచికరమైన** | “delightful” | OK | | monte | noun “mountain” (accusative) | **పర్వతాన్ని** | “the mountain (ACC)” | OK | | ch'è | relative pronoun + copula “which is” | **అది** | “that / it” | OK | | principio | noun “source / origin” | **మూలం** | “source / origin” | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | **మరియు** | “and” | OK | | cagion | noun “cause” | **కారణం** | “cause” | OK | | di | preposition “of” (genitive) | **కు** | “of / for” | OK | | tutta | universal quantifier “all / every” | **మొత్తం** | “all / every” | OK | | gioia | noun “joy” (dative) | **ఆనందానికి** | “to joy” | OK |
---
### Items Flagged
- **UNNECESSARY**: `il` – Telugu does not use definite articles, so the article is naturally omitted. No other tokens are missing or incorrectly rendered.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Telugu script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Telugu text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
